newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady despite crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady despite crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady late afternoon on Monday despite big losses to crude values as the market consolidated at around the $25.00 per barrel mark, traders said.
"Gas oil is steady, it's consolidating around the $25.00 mark, and where it goes from here depends on what happens this evening on the physical market," said a trader.
May gas oil swaps were last quoted $25.10/$25.20 per barrel, up from Friday's quotes at $25.05/$25.15. May traded earlier in the day at $25.10, brokers said.
On Friday, Brent crude levels on London's International Petroleum Exchange fell to a session low of $17.88 per barrel, easing 32 cents.
Traders said alot depends on what happens this evening on the physical market in determining the new course of the gas oil market.
If the group of traders, who have together bought more than 18 million barrels since March 3, stop their support then the market will see a big downward correction, they said.
So far the traders have chosen to bring the market down gradually by bidding at successively lower prices from a high of $28.75 in mid-March to a low of $25.50 last Friday.
Traders said the market is under downward pressure following results of the latest Indian tender.
India bought around 270,000 tonnes for June delivery, well below traders expectations of 600,000 tonnes.
The front month May jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade narrowed to value at around flat from around minus 50 cents about one week ago.
Fuel oil swaps were slightly lower, with May seen at $98.25/$99.75, brokers said.
